speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when your tympanoplasty was performed and how long you have been experiencing this shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any tenderness or swelling when I press on the area just in front of your earlobe, and does chewing or opening your mouth wide trigger a clicking sensation or pain in that same region?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you notice any clicking or popping sensations in the jaw joint when you open or close your mouth, and is there any tenderness to palpation over the temporomandibular joint itself? I need to rule out temporomandibular joint dysfunction as the source of your referred ear pain.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: History of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. Underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks prior. Social history: Works as a cashier at a local department store.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain radiate from the jaw joint into the ear, and do you experience any locking or limited range of motion when opening your mouth? I need to confirm if this is temporomandibular joint dysfunction causing referred otalgia.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you deny facial tenderness and neck pain, I need to rule out local pathology in the ear itself. Is there any visible discharge, redness, or tenderness when I gently pull on your right earlobe? REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal otoscopy and the specific trigger of eating, I suspect a neuroma or nerve irritation from the surgery. Do you experience any numbness or tingling sensation in the ear canal or on the tragus when the pain occurs?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: You have denied numbness or tingling, which makes a nerve injury less likely. Given the pain is triggered by eating and you have no signs of infection or TMJ dysfunction, I suspect a neuroma or neuralgia involving the auriculotemporal nerve. REQUEST TEST: MRI of the temporal bone

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal imaging and otoscopy ruling out structural causes, I suspect auriculotemporal neuralgia exacerbated by your stress and poor sleep. Let's try a trial of carbamazepine to see if the shooting pain subsides.
